userSpecifiedSources: NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 (G02135, doi:10.7265/a98x-0f50); NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory CO2, CH4, N2O and SF6 trends (gml.noaa.gov/ccgg/trends, with Scripps Institution of Oceanography for Mauna Loa CO2); NOAA OISST v2.1 daily 0.25-degree SST via NOAA PSL, cross-checked against NCEI and NOAA CPC; ERA5 daily global 2 m air temperature from the Copernicus Climate Change Service (Climate Pulse); NOAA CPC ONI, RONI and daily AO/NAO/PNA/AAO; NOAA GML AGGI expressions; NOAA NCEI TSI Climate Data Record v3 and PDO index. Built daily by scripts/build.py in https://github.com/yasumorishima/earth-vital-signs, which publishes nothing unless every check passes.

sea_ice_extent_daily.csv.description: Daily sea ice extent for the Arctic, the Antarctic and both combined (NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4), with the anomaly, the rank for the calendar day, a record-low flag and the change from a year earlier.

columns.hemisphere: north (Arctic), south (Antarctic) or global (north + south, on days both are reported)
columns.extent_mkm2: Sea ice extent in million square kilometres (area with at least 15% ice concentration)
columns.missing_mkm2: Area with missing satellite data, million square kilometres (0 on almost all days)
columns.extent_5day_mean_mkm2: Trailing 5-day mean of extent (this day and the 4 before) as used in NSIDC charts; empty where those 5 days are not all present (every-other-day era before 1987-08)
columns.extent_anom_1991_2020_mkm2: extent_mkm2 minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), million square kilometres
columns.rank_lowest_for_day: Rank of extent_mkm2 among the same calendar day of every year up to and including this one (1 = lowest), counting only this year and earlier years, so later years never change it (a recent day can still move while its value is inside the source revision window). Feb 29 is ranked among leap years only
columns.record_low_for_day: True when extent is below the same calendar day of every earlier year (a record low for the date); empty until 10 earlier years exist for that day
columns.yoy_change_mkm2: extent_mkm2 minus the value on the same date one year earlier; empty if that day was not observed (and on Feb 29)
columns.change_7d_mkm2: extent_mkm2 minus the value 7 days earlier, million square kilometres (melt or freeze-up pace; divide by 7 for a daily rate); empty before 1987-08, when the record is every other day

co2_daily_mauna_loa.csv.description: Daily mean atmospheric CO2 at Mauna Loa Observatory (NOAA GML); days without valid measurements are absent. With the change from a year earlier and a record-high flag.

columns.decimal_date: Date as a decimal year, as published by NOAA GML
columns.co2_ppm: Daily mean CO2 mole fraction, parts per million (dry air)
columns.yoy_change_ppm: co2_ppm minus the value on the same date one year earlier, ppm; empty when either day has no measurement (Mauna Loa has gaps, e.g. 2025-09-27 to 10-06)
columns.record_high: True when co2_ppm is above every earlier daily value in the file

greenhouse_gases_monthly.csv.description: Monthly greenhouse gas averages from NOAA GML in long format (one row per series and month).

columns.series: co2_mlo (Mauna Loa, ppm), co2_global (ppm), ch4_global (ppb), n2o_global (ppb) or sf6_global (ppt)
columns.date: First day of the month, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.average: Monthly mean in the series' unit; empty where NOAA reports missing
columns.deseasonalized: Monthly value with the average seasonal cycle removed, as published by NOAA GML
columns.interpolated: co2_mlo only, from 1974-05: True where NOAA filled a missing month by interpolation (negative stdev in the source file); empty for other series and for the Scripps months before 1974-05
columns.yoy_change: average minus the same month one year earlier, in the series' unit (the annual growth)

sst_daily.csv.description: Daily area-weighted mean sea surface temperature for 11 ocean regions, computed from the full NOAA OISST v2.1 0.25-degree grid (cos-latitude weights, ocean cells only), with anomalies, records and two climate indices (Indian Ocean Dipole, relative Niño 3.4).

columns.world_60s_60n: Mean SST over 60S-60N, all longitudes (the near-global series least affected by sea ice), degrees Celsius
columns.north_atlantic_0_60n_0_80w: Mean SST over North Atlantic, 0-60N, 80W-0, degrees Celsius
columns.world_90s_90n: Mean SST over the whole globe, 90S-90N (cells under sea ice carry OISST's freezing-point value), degrees Celsius
columns.tropics_20s_20n: Mean SST over tropics, 20S-20N, all longitudes, degrees Celsius
columns.north_pacific_20n_60n_120e_110w: Mean SST over North Pacific, 20N-60N, 120E-110W, degrees Celsius
columns.nino12_0_10s_90w_80w: Mean SST over Niño 1+2 box, 0-10S, 90W-80W (NOAA CPC definition), degrees Celsius
columns.nino3_5n_5s_150w_90w: Mean SST over Niño 3 box, 5N-5S, 150W-90W (NOAA CPC definition), degrees Celsius
columns.nino34_5n_5s_170w_120w: Mean SST over Niño 3.4 box, 5N-5S, 170W-120W (NOAA CPC definition; the main ENSO box), degrees Celsius
columns.nino4_5n_5s_160e_150w: Mean SST over Niño 4 box, 5N-5S, 160E-150W (NOAA CPC definition), degrees Celsius
columns.iod_west_10s_10n_50e_70e: Mean SST over western pole of the Indian Ocean Dipole, 10S-10N, 50E-70E (Saji et al. 1999), degrees Celsius
columns.iod_east_10s_0_90e_110e: Mean SST over eastern pole of the Indian Ocean Dipole, 10S-0, 90E-110E (Saji et al. 1999), degrees Celsius
columns.world_60s_60n_anom_1991_2020: world_60s_60n minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.north_atlantic_0_60n_0_80w_anom_1991_202: north_atlantic_0_60n_0_80w minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.world_90s_90n_anom_1991_2020: world_90s_90n minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.tropics_20s_20n_anom_1991_2020: tropics_20s_20n minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.north_pacific_20n_60n_120e_110w_anom_199: north_pacific_20n_60n_120e_110w minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.nino12_0_10s_90w_80w_anom_1991_2020: nino12_0_10s_90w_80w minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.nino3_5n_5s_150w_90w_anom_1991_2020: nino3_5n_5s_150w_90w minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.nino34_5n_5s_170w_120w_anom_1991_2020: nino34_5n_5s_170w_120w minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.nino4_5n_5s_160e_150w_anom_1991_2020: nino4_5n_5s_160e_150w minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.iod_west_10s_10n_50e_70e_anom_1991_2020: iod_west_10s_10n_50e_70e minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.iod_east_10s_0_90e_110e_anom_1991_2020: iod_east_10s_0_90e_110e minus its 1991-2020 mean for the same calendar day (Feb 29 uses Feb 28's normal), degrees Celsius
columns.world_60s_60n_rank_warmest_for_day: Rank of world_60s_60n among the same calendar day of every year up to and including this one (1 = warmest), counting only this year and earlier years, so later years never change it (a recent day can still move while its value is inside the source revision window). Feb 29 is ranked among leap years only
columns.world_60s_60n_record_warm_for_day: True when world_60s_60n is warmer than on the same calendar day of every earlier year; empty until 10 earlier years exist for that day
columns.world_90s_90n_rank_warmest_for_day: Rank of world_90s_90n among the same calendar day of every year up to and including this one (1 = warmest), counting only this year and earlier years, so later years never change it (a recent day can still move while its value is inside the source revision window). Feb 29 is ranked among leap years only
columns.world_90s_90n_record_warm_for_day: True when world_90s_90n is warmer than on the same calendar day of every earlier year; empty until 10 earlier years exist for that day
columns.dmi: Dipole Mode Index of the Indian Ocean Dipole: western-pole anomaly minus eastern-pole anomaly (Saji et al. 1999), degrees Celsius; positive = positive IOD
columns.nino34_minus_tropics_anom: Niño 3.4 anomaly minus the tropical (20S-20N) mean anomaly, degrees Celsius. The relative Niño 3.4 behind NOAA CPC's RONI, without CPC's variance scaling or 3-month averaging
columns.amo_ts06: Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation index as revised by Trenberth & Shea (2006, GRL 33, L12704): North Atlantic (0-60N, 80W-0) anomaly minus the 60S-60N anomaly, daily and unsmoothed, degrees Celsius. Removing the near-global mean keeps global warming out of the index
columns.world_60s_60n_ytd_anom_1991_2020: Mean of world_60s_60n_anom_1991_2020 from 1 January to this day (year-to-date), degrees Celsius; empty in 1981, which starts in September
columns.world_60s_60n_ytd_rank_warmest_for_day: Rank of the year-to-date mean among the same calendar day of every year up to and including this one (1 = warmest), counting only this year and earlier years, so later years never change it (a recent day can still move while its value is inside the source revision window). Feb 29 is ranked among leap years only
columns.world_60s_60n_ytd_record_warm_for_day: True when the year-to-date mean is warmer than at the same date of every earlier year; empty until 10 earlier years exist

air_temperature_daily.csv.description: Daily global mean 2 m air temperature from ERA5 (Copernicus Climate Change Service, via Climate Pulse), 1940 to present, with C3S's 1991-2020 climatology and anomaly, the rank for the calendar day and a record flag.

columns.global_2t: Daily global mean near-surface (2 m) air temperature from ERA5 hourly values, degrees Celsius
columns.global_2t_clim_1991_2020: C3S daily climatology for 1991-2020 for this calendar day, degrees Celsius
columns.global_2t_anom_1991_2020: global_2t minus global_2t_clim_1991_2020 as published by C3S, degrees Celsius
columns.status: final, or preliminary for the most recent days (based on ERA5 data not yet final; usually revised slightly within a few days)
columns.global_rank_warmest_for_day: Rank of global_2t among the same calendar day of every year up to and including this one (1 = warmest), counting only this year and earlier years, so later years never change it (a recent day can still move while its value is inside the source revision window). Feb 29 is ranked among leap years only
columns.global_record_warm_for_day: True when global_2t is warmer than on the same calendar day of every earlier year; empty until 10 earlier years exist for that day
columns.global_2t_anom_preindustrial: Anomaly above the 1850-1900 (pre-industrial) level, the reference of the Paris Agreement, as C3S computes it: global_2t_anom_1991_2020 plus C3S's day-of-year offset 0.88 + 0.05 sin(2pi(n-0.5)/365) + 0.07 cos(2pi(n-0.5)/365) (0.79-0.97), not a flat 0.88. Its yearly means reproduce C3S's published 1.48 (2023), 1.60 (2024) and 1.47 (2025), degrees Celsius
columns.global_above_1_5c_preindustrial: True when global_2t_anom_preindustrial is above 1.5. A single day above 1.5 C is not a breach of the Paris Agreement, which refers to warming averaged over about 20 years
columns.global_above_2_0c_preindustrial: True when global_2t_anom_preindustrial is above 2.0 (first on 2023-11-17 in ERA5)
columns.global_2t_anom_preindustrial_365d: Mean of global_2t_anom_preindustrial over this day and the 364 before (a trailing 365-day mean), degrees Celsius; empty for the first 364 days of the record (until 1940-12-30)
columns.global_ytd_anom_preindustrial: Mean of global_2t_anom_preindustrial from 1 January to this day (year-to-date); on 31 December it is the annual mean, degrees Celsius
columns.global_ytd_rank_warmest_for_day: Rank of the year-to-date mean among the same calendar day of every year up to and including this one (1 = warmest year so far), counting only this year and earlier years, so later years never change it (a recent day can still move while its value is inside the source revision window). Feb 29 is ranked among leap years only
columns.global_ytd_record_warm_for_day: True when the year-to-date mean is warmer than at the same date of every earlier year; empty until 10 earlier years exist

enso_monthly.csv.description: El Niño-Southern Oscillation indices from NOAA CPC: the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) and the Relative ONI (RONI), which NOAA uses for official ENSO monitoring per NWS Public Information Statement 26-05. One row per overlapping 3-month season.

columns.date: First day of the centre month of the 3-month season (e.g. DJF 1950 -> 1950-01-01)
columns.season: 3-month season label as published by CPC (DJF, JFM, ... NDJ)
columns.oni_total_c: Niño 3.4 SST from ERSST v6 (CPC's current ONI file), 3-month mean, degrees Celsius
columns.oni_anom: ONI: 3-month mean Niño 3.4 anomaly as published by CPC, degrees Celsius. El Niño conditions at +0.5 or above, La Niña at -0.5 or below
columns.roni_anom: RONI: ONI-style index of the Niño 3.4 anomaly relative to the tropical mean, as published by CPC, degrees Celsius
columns.oni_episode: el_nino, la_nina or neutral by NOAA CPC's rule on ONI: the one-decimal value at or above +0.5 (or at or below -0.5) for at least 5 consecutive overlapping seasons. Empty while a run is still open with fewer than 5 seasons (undetermined). Checked every run against the colours of CPC's own table. Retrospective: a season's label uses up to 4 later seasons, so do not use it as a feature known at that date
columns.roni_episode: el_nino, la_nina or neutral by NOAA CPC's rule on RONI: the one-decimal value at or above +0.5 (or at or below -0.5) for at least 5 consecutive overlapping seasons. Empty while a run is still open with fewer than 5 seasons (undetermined). Checked every run against the colours of CPC's own table. Retrospective: a season's label uses up to 4 later seasons, so do not use it as a feature known at that date

atmosphere_indices_daily.csv.description: Daily standardized atmospheric circulation indices from NOAA CPC: Arctic Oscillation, North Atlantic Oscillation, Pacific-North American pattern and Antarctic Oscillation. CPC's files are named after NCEP's CDAS analysis, which NCEP replaced with CORe on 2026-03-18; values from then on may come from the new system.

columns.ao: Arctic Oscillation index (1000 hPa height), standardized, unitless
columns.nao: North Atlantic Oscillation index (500 hPa height), standardized, unitless
columns.pna: Pacific-North American pattern index (500 hPa height), standardized, unitless
columns.aao: Antarctic Oscillation (Southern Annular Mode) index (700 hPa height), standardized, unitless; from 1979

climate_drivers_monthly.csv.description: Monthly drivers of global temperature: effective radiative forcing of CO2, CH4 and N2O (NOAA AGGI method), total solar irradiance (NOAA CDR) and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (NOAA NCEI).

columns.date: First day of the month, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.erf_co2_wm2: Effective radiative forcing of CO2 since 1750, W m-2, from the global monthly CO2, CH4 and N2O in greenhouse_gases_monthly with the expressions of NOAA's Annual Greenhouse Gas Index (Forster et al. 2021, Smith et al. 2021); from 2001, when the global N2O series starts. Annual means reproduce NOAA's AGGI table within 0.004
columns.erf_ch4_wm2: Effective radiative forcing of CH4 since 1750, W m-2 (same method)
columns.erf_n2o_wm2: Effective radiative forcing of N2O since 1750, W m-2 (same method)
columns.erf_co2_ch4_n2o_wm2: Sum of the three, W m-2. Excludes the halocarbons (about 0.4 W m-2 in NOAA's AGGI), aerosols and ozone, so it is not the total forcing
columns.tsi_wm2: Total solar irradiance at 1 AU, W m-2, monthly mean from NOAA's TSI Climate Data Record v3 (NNLTSI model, Coddington, Lean, Lindholm et al., doi:10.25921/k2ff-p712); released about once a year, so the latest months are empty until the next release
columns.pdo: Pacific Decadal Oscillation index from NOAA NCEI (ERSST v5 anomalies projected on the Mantua PDO pattern), unitless

climate_monthly_panel.csv.description: Every indicator side by side, one row per month from 1950: monthly means of the daily tables plus the monthly gases and ENSO indices. Ready for correlation, regression or forecasting. Daily-derived columns are filled only when at least 90% of the month's days are present (40% for sea ice, observed every other day before 1987-08); empty otherwise.

columns.date: First day of the month, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.sst_world_60s_60n_anom: Monthly mean of sst_daily.world_60s_60n_anom_1991_2020, degrees Celsius
columns.sst_dmi: Monthly mean of sst_daily.dmi (Indian Ocean Dipole), degrees Celsius
columns.sea_ice_north_mkm2: Monthly mean Arctic sea ice extent, million square kilometres
columns.sea_ice_south_mkm2: Monthly mean Antarctic sea ice extent, million square kilometres
columns.sea_ice_north_anom_mkm2: Monthly mean Arctic extent anomaly against 1991-2020, million km2
columns.sea_ice_south_anom_mkm2: Monthly mean Antarctic extent anomaly against 1991-2020, million km2
columns.ao: Monthly mean of the daily Arctic Oscillation index
columns.nao: Monthly mean of the daily North Atlantic Oscillation index
columns.pna: Monthly mean of the daily Pacific-North American index
columns.aao: Monthly mean of the daily Antarctic Oscillation index
columns.co2_mlo_ppm: Monthly mean CO2 at Mauna Loa, ppm
columns.co2_global_ppm: Monthly global marine surface CO2, ppm
columns.oni_anom: ONI for the 3-month season centred on this month
columns.roni_anom: RONI for the 3-month season centred on this month
columns.sst_amo_ts06: Monthly mean of sst_daily.amo_ts06 (Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation), degrees Celsius
columns.roni_episode: enso_monthly.roni_episode for that season (retrospective; see that column)
